agent.Advanced view hint: Every installation found, with its processes, path, owner and install method.
agent.Base URL hint: Give the agent the settings below. Requests that arrive at this URL always go to the provider selected above, whatever model they name.
agent.Bound provider cooling down: The bound provider is out of rotation, requests go to the fallbacks
agent.Built-in hint: This agent is on the model it comes with. Gateway forwards nothing for it and only watches what it does.
agent.Built-in model restored: Put back on its own model
agent.Claude Code config hint: The same variables can live in the "env" block of ~/.claude/settings.json, so every session picks them up without exporting anything.
agent.Claude Desktop sandbox hint: Claude Desktop runs its Cowork and Code sessions in a sandbox of its own, where 127.0.0.1 is that sandbox rather than this host. The URL above names this machine on its own network instead, and Gateway answers there as well as on loopback.
agent.Client auth token hint: This provider forwards the agent's own credentials, so no token is set: the agent keeps the sign-in it already has.
agent.Codex CLI config hint: The base URL can also be a model provider in ~/.codex/config.toml, selected with model_provider. Its wire_api has to be "responses", the only wire format Codex still speaks.
agent.Direct mode hint: The provider's own base URL and key are written into the agent's configuration. Switching to another provider rewrites the file, and the agent has to be restarted to pick it up.
agent.Failed to write the agent configuration: Failed to write the agent configuration
agent.Fallback hint: Providers tried, in the order picked, when the bound one cannot answer.
agent.Gateway mode hint: The agent is pointed at the local proxy, so switching to another provider takes effect on the next request without restarting the agent.
agent.Gateway only hint: Codex speaks only the OpenAI Responses API. Gateway serves it by translating to the chat completions this provider answers, so Codex cannot be pointed at it directly.
agent.Gemini CLI config hint: The Gemini CLI reads no base URL from a settings file: the endpoint is GOOGLE_GEMINI_BASE_URL in ~/.gemini/.env, with GEMINI_API_KEY beside it and "security.auth.selectedType": "gemini-api-key" in ~/.gemini/settings.json. A project of its own .env is read first, and that one wins.
agent.Gemini gateway only hint: The Gemini CLI speaks only Google's generateContent API, which no provider here serves. Gateway serves it by translating to the API the provider answers, so the CLI cannot be pointed at a provider directly.
agent.Install an AI agent on this machine, the: Install an AI agent on this machine, then scan again
agent.No agent records yet - patch an agent to: No activity yet - turn on monitoring for an agent to start collecting it
agent.No agent sessions yet - patch an agent t: No sessions yet - turn on monitoring for an agent to start collecting them
agent.No other provider speaks this API: No other provider speaks this API
agent.No usage yet: No requests have been relayed for this agent yet
agent.Not installed hint: Agents Gateway works with that were not found on this machine. Install one with a package manager this host already has, or open its vendor's page.
agent.Preview hint: What Gateway would write, with the keys masked. Everything else in these files is left as it is.
agent.Provider speaks another API: This agent speaks the {protocol} API, which the bound provider does not. A direct binding needs both to speak the same one: pick another provider, or route this agent through the gateway, which translates.
agent.Read from the agent's own logs: Read from the agent's own logs
agent.Records are kept in memory only and are: Records are kept in memory only and are lost when Gateway restarts
agent.Restore confirm hint: Puts back the provider settings this agent had before Gateway first wrote them, and leaves every other setting untouched.
agent.Running in a container: Gateway is running in a container
agent.Running in a container detail: Agents are found by reading the home directories of the machine Gateway runs on, and in a container that is the container's own filesystem rather than the host's. Install Gateway on the host to see the agents installed there. Providers and LLM Records work either way.
agent.Start app hint: Opens the app on the machine Gateway runs on.
agent.Start console hint: Opens a console window running the CLI on the machine Gateway runs on.
agent.Still calling Gateway: This agent is set to its own model, but its configuration still points at Gateway, so every request fails. Put the configuration back.
agent.Stop hint: Ends every process of this installation, losing whatever it is working on.
agent.Switch takes effect at once: Picking another provider above rewrites this file at once, so switching takes one click.
agent.Token hint: Gateway authenticates upstream with the provider's own key. This value is Gateway's own relay token, which a request from another machine has to carry.
agent.Transcript truncated: Some of this session was too large to show, so what follows is not all of it
agent.Turn on monitoring to collect activity: Turn on monitoring to collect activity
agent.Upgrade hint: Replaces this installation with the latest version, through the package manager that installed it. Restart the agent afterwards to run the new one.
agent.Write confirm hint: Gateway writes the selected provider into this agent's own configuration file, replacing the file in one step. Restart any session that is already running.
agent.opencode config hint: opencode reads no base URL from the environment: the endpoint is a "provider" entry in ~/.config/opencode/opencode.json, loaded through @ai-sdk/openai-compatible and selected with "model": "<provider>/<model>".

agentConfig.Add MCP server hint: Gateway writes the server into each agent's own configuration file, in that agent's own format. Restart a session that is already running to pick it up.
agentConfig.Add to hint: Every agent picked here gets the same server.
agentConfig.Command hint: The executable the agent spawns, e.g. npx or uvx.
agentConfig.Copy mode hint: The agent gets its own copy. Fetching the source again offers an update rather than changing it underneath.
agentConfig.Credentials are masked here: Credentials are masked in this view. A copy carries the real values.
agentConfig.Delete description: This removes it from the agent's own configuration, here:
agentConfig.Delete for good description: This erases it from the recycle bin, and it cannot be restored afterwards.
agentConfig.Delete undo hint: It goes to Gateway's recycle bin first, so this can be undone.
agentConfig.Diverged detail: The source has changed and so has this copy. Updating replaces what was changed here, and puts it in the recycle bin.
agentConfig.Edited here detail: This copy differs from the source it came from, and that source has not changed since.
agentConfig.Failed to add this MCP server: Failed to add this MCP server
agentConfig.Failed to add this source: This source could not be added
agentConfig.Failed to install: The skills could not be installed
agentConfig.Failed to plan this copy: Failed to work out what this copy would do
agentConfig.Failed to read agent configuration: Failed to read the agents' configuration
agentConfig.Failed to read the recycle bin: Failed to read the recycle bin
agentConfig.Failed to read the skill sources: The skill sources could not be read
agentConfig.Failed to read this source: This source could not be read
agentConfig.Failed to remove this source: This source could not be removed
agentConfig.From a plugin detail: Shipped by the {plugin} plugin. Uninstall the plugin to remove it.
agentConfig.From a project detail: Kept in the project at {project}, not in the agent's own skills directory.
agentConfig.Gateway does not know where this agent k: Gateway does not know where this agent keeps these
agentConfig.GitHub source hint: owner/repo, or the address of a repository, a branch or a folder inside one.
agentConfig.Install into hint: Every agent picked here gets the same skills, each in its own skills directory.
agentConfig.Install skills hint: Pick a source, pick what it holds, and put it into the agents you name. Anything with a SKILL.md in it can be a source.
agentConfig.Link mode hint: The agent points at Gateway's copy of the source, so every agent linked to it moves together when the source is fetched again.
agentConfig.Linked detail: A link to {target}, not a copy. It follows whatever that folder holds.
agentConfig.Local source hint: A folder on this machine holding skill folders.
agentConfig.Managed by Gateway detail: Registered by Gateway's agent monitoring. Turn monitoring off on the Agents page to remove it.
agentConfig.No MCP servers yet: This agent has no MCP servers yet
agentConfig.No agents found: No agents found on this machine
agentConfig.No agents found detail: Gateway reads the configuration of the agents installed where it runs. Inside a container it sees the container's own filesystem, not the host's.
agentConfig.No instructions yet: This agent has no instructions yet
agentConfig.No other agent on this machine can recei: No other agent on this machine can receive these.
agentConfig.No skills yet: This agent has no skills yet
agentConfig.No sources yet: No sources yet. Add a GitHub repository, an archive or a folder to install from.
agentConfig.Not installed detail: Gateway found this configuration on disk but did not detect an installation of the agent.
agentConfig.Not written yet detail: This agent would read this file, but nobody has written it. Editing it creates it.
agentConfig.Nothing deleted detail: Skills, MCP servers and instructions deleted on this page wait here for 30 days before they are really gone.
agentConfig.Out of date detail: {agents} hold a newer version of this.
agentConfig.Page description: The skills, MCP servers and instructions each agent on this machine keeps in its own configuration files. Compare them side by side, and copy them from one agent to another.
agentConfig.Pick the agents to copy into: pick the agents to copy into
agentConfig.Prompt editor hint: What this agent is told before every session. It is saved to the agent's own file, and a session already running has to be restarted to pick it up.
agentConfig.Prompt placeholder: Nothing here yet. Anything written here is read by this agent at the start of every session.
agentConfig.Recycle bin hint: What deleting removed, kept for 30 days. Restoring puts it back where it was.
agentConfig.Remove source description: Gateway drops its copy of this source. Skills already installed from it stay where they are.
agentConfig.Restore as a replacement description: Something is at that path again. It is moved to the recycle bin in its turn, and this item takes its place.
agentConfig.Shared with: The same files are read by {agents}.
agentConfig.This file is read-only for Gateway: Gateway does not write this agent's configuration file
agentConfig.This source holds no skills: Nothing in this source has a SKILL.md in it.
agentConfig.Up to date detail: This holds exactly what its source holds.
agentConfig.Update available detail: The source this was copied from has changed since.
agentConfig.Update description: This replaces the skill with the current content of:
agentConfig.Update undo hint: The version it replaces goes to the recycle bin, so this can be undone.
agentConfig.Upload source hint: A .zip or .tar.gz of skill folders, from this computer.
agentConfig.Version detail: A digest of the skill's files. Two agents holding the same digest hold the same version.

audit.Billing detail: {billed} input tokens billed for about {estimate} sent. Four characters to the token is rough, so only a wide gap means anything.
audit.Billing unstable: Two byte-identical requests were billed {first} and {second} input tokens. The same prompt has to cost the same twice.
audit.Cache detail: {hits} of {sample} long prompts came back with cache tokens on them.
audit.Cache never reported: None of {sample} long prompts came back with any cache tokens, so each was billed as fresh input.
audit.Cache probe none: The probe asked for a cache and the answer accounted for none of it, so the whole prompt was billed as fresh input.
audit.Cache probe ok: {written} tokens written, {read} read back on the identical second request.
audit.Cache probe written only: {written} tokens were written but none were read back a second later.
audit.Every model has a rate: Every model this provider served has a published rate.
audit.Failed over hint: Attempts this provider lost, which another one in the chain then answered. They are not counted as its requests.
audit.Identity different: Asked for {asked} and the answer named {answered}.
audit.Identity ok: Answered as {answered}. Echoing a name back is easy, so this is a floor rather than a proof.
audit.No model name came back: The answer carried no model name.
audit.No traffic in this window: No relayed request in this window.
audit.No vendor header: No response header of this vendor's own API came back. A relay may simply strip them.
audit.Not probed yet auto: Not probed yet. A provider is probed when it is added, when its endpoint or key changes, and once if it has never been.
audit.Not probed yet manual: Not probed yet. Probing only runs when it is asked for.
audit.Nothing could report a cache: Nothing here could have reported a cache: the OpenAI protocol does not account for one, and short prompts are not eligible.
audit.Nothing to audit yet: No relayed request to read yet
audit.Nothing to audit yet detail: The audit reads records the proxy already kept. Point an agent at a provider and its first requests will show up here.
audit.Nothing was relayed in this window: Nothing was relayed in this window.
audit.Only the newest records were read: This window holds more records than one audit reads, so only the newest {count} were counted.
audit.Page description: What each upstream looks like from here, from both sides. Traffic reads records Gateway already kept and costs nothing. A probe asks the upstream directly, with four short requests whose right answers the vendor's own API documents, and spends a few cents of that provider's credit. Every figure names what it was measured over, because a rate over four requests is not a finding.
audit.Pricing detail: {unpriced} of {sample} answered requests used a model no price list names.
audit.Probe cost hint: What the probe itself spent of this provider's credit.
audit.Probe failed: The probe could not be completed: {reason}
audit.Probe mode detail: A probe sends four short requests and spends a few cents of the probed provider's own credit. Change this under Settings.
audit.Probing is off: Probing is turned off, so nothing here was asked directly.
audit.Recording is off detail: The audit has nothing to read while llmRecordMode is "off". Metadata alone is enough for every check here; prompts do not have to be stored.
audit.Stream complete: Every event this API documents arrived, in order.
audit.This question could not be asked: This request did not go through, so the question stays unanswered.
audit.Too few to measure: Fewer than {min} requests, too few to read anything into.
audit.Tools none: The tool call was forced and the answer contained none.
audit.Tools ok: The forced call came back with both levels of the schema filled in.
audit.Tools partial: The tool was called but the nested fields it requires were not filled in.
audit.What this cannot tell you: These are the upstream's own numbers. They show what it reported, not what it ran.

general.Cannot connect to the server, please che: Cannot connect to the server, please check that the backend is running
general.Casbin Gateway installs updates from the: Casbin Gateway installs updates from the nightly build of master
general.GitHub could not be reached, if this mac: GitHub could not be reached, if this machine needs a proxy to reach the internet, set one and try again
general.Leave this page open, it reloads itself: Leave this page open, it reloads itself when the new version is up
general.Name: Name
general.No build is published for this platform,: No build is published for this platform, so the update has to be done by hand
general.Sorry, you do not have permission to acc: Sorry, you do not have permission to access this page or logged in status invalid.
general.The new version did not start, check the: The new version did not start, check the Gateway log
general.This Gateway cannot find its own executa: This Gateway cannot find its own executable, so the update has to be done by hand
general.This executable sits where it cannot be: This executable sits where it cannot be replaced, so the update has to be done by hand
general.This is a read-only demo site!: This is a read-only demo site!

llm.Bodies are not stored detail: llmRecordMode is "metadata", so the prompts, tool schemas and messages behind these rows were never kept. Store them from now on to inspect them.
llm.Bodies are stored: Prompts and responses are being stored
llm.Bodies are stored detail: llmRecordMode is "full", so the prompts, tool schemas and messages of every relayed request are kept, with the credentials removed. Record metadata only, or stop recording, to keep less.
llm.Body is not JSON: The stored body is not valid JSON, so it is shown as it was captured.
llm.Body not stored: The request body was not stored: llmRecordMode is "metadata".
llm.Body too large to store: The request body was larger than the capture limit and was not stored.
llm.Body was shortened: The body was over the capture limit, so its longest strings were cut. Every message, tool and parameter is still listed. Raise llmRecordMaxPayloadBytes to keep more.
llm.Cache breakpoint detail: This block carries cache_control, so the prompt cache is written up to here.
llm.List prices, see llmPricingFile: List prices - override them with llmPricingFile.
llm.Mode full: full - metadata and sanitized request body
llm.Mode {mode}, kept for {days} days, up to: Mode {mode}, kept for {days} days, up to {max} records
llm.No error message: The upstream gave no error message
llm.No parameters: This request carried no parameters of its own.
llm.No price for this model: No price is configured for this model
llm.No records yet: No records yet - send a request through the LLM gateway.
llm.No system prompt: This request carried no system prompt.
llm.No tools: The model was offered no tools.
llm.Recording is off detail: Recording is turned off, so nothing about a relayed request is being kept. Metadata is who called which model with which outcome; bodies are the prompts themselves.
llm.Records were dropped: {count} records were dropped because the write queue was full. Raise llmRecordQueueCapacity if this keeps happening.
llm.{count} of these requests have no list p: {count} of these requests have no list price

provider.API Key hint: The stored key is never sent back to the browser. Leave *** as it is to keep the current key, or clear the field to remove it.
provider.API Key ownership hint: Stored by Gateway and never handed to an agent.
provider.Any model hint: Leave this empty to accept every model name, which is what a provider that forwards the caller's login usually wants.
provider.Ask an endpoint of my own: Ask an endpoint of my own
provider.Balance URL hint: A path, resolved against the provider's own base URL. An absolute URL works too, but it has to stay on that same host.
provider.Balance description: What the vendor says is left on the account this provider bills. Gateway knows the endpoint of a few vendors; for the rest, and for aggregator sites, name one here.
provider.Balance headers hint: One NAME=VALUE per line. {{token}} stands for the balance token and {{apiKey}} for the provider's own key, so neither has to be written out twice.
provider.Balance token hint: Only for a vendor whose balance endpoint does not take the inference key, as an aggregator's system token does not. Stored like the API key and never sent back to the browser.
provider.Claude subscription detail: The sign-in Claude Code already has, forwarded upstream. No API key, nothing to fill in. Codex is the exception: it signs in against an API Gateway does not relay.
provider.Client auth hint: Requests are forwarded with the credentials the client sent, so an agent already signed in with a subscription keeps its own login and no key is stored here. Codex is the exception: its ChatGPT sign-in speaks a different API.
provider.Client auth usage hint: Only the base URL is set: a token here would replace the sign-in the client already has.
provider.Connectivity hint: A read-only probe against the upstream, which costs nothing and answers whether this key works. It also runs once when the form is submitted.
provider.Currency hint: What the numbers are counted in, after the scale is applied.
provider.Custom endpoint hint: Leave this off for a vendor Gateway already knows the balance endpoint of.
provider.Custom vendor detail: Any OpenAI- or Anthropic-compatible API. You give it a base URL and a key.
provider.Icon hint: The site the vendor's icon is taken from, or an image URL. Leave it empty to take it from the base URL.
provider.Model routing hint: Requests that arrive here are routed by the model name they carry, to the enabled provider with the smallest priority value that serves it. To send one agent's requests to this provider whatever model they name, bind the provider on the agent's page instead.
provider.Models hint: The model names this provider serves, used to route requests that arrive by model name.
provider.Name hint: Whatever you will recognise this account by. A second account with the same vendor gets a number.
provider.No models hint: With no model named, nothing that arrives by model name will be routed here. Press Fetch models, or type the names this provider should serve. An empty list only means "any model" for a provider that forwards the caller's own login.
provider.No providers yet detail: A provider is your own vendor account: a base URL, the models it serves, and either an API key or the caller's own login forwarded upstream. Add one, then bind it to an agent to route that agent's requests through it.
provider.No vendor matches: No vendor matches that. Pick Custom to enter one by hand.
provider.Notes hint: For whoever reads this later: which account the key belongs to, when it expires, who pays for it.
provider.Nothing to test: There is nothing to test yet
provider.Page description: One endpoint in front of your model vendors. Gateway holds the API key, so the agents never have it — or forwards the agent's own sign-in and holds nothing.
provider.Paste a provider link hint: Vendors publish these as "add to CC Switch" buttons. Gateway reads the same link and fills the form in below, and stores nothing until you confirm.
provider.Path hint: A dotted path into the answer, where a number indexes an array: balance_infos.0.total_balance.
provider.Preset hint: Fills in the paths for a family of sites, so they do not have to be read out of the vendor's API documentation.
provider.Priority hint: Smaller number means higher priority, 0 is the highest; when multiple providers serve the same model, the one with the smaller value is used first.
provider.Save anyway hint: The upstream did not accept this provider. Fix it, or press {action} again to store it as it is.
provider.Scale hint: Divides every number read, for a vendor that counts in an internal unit of its own. New API counts in 1/500000 of a dollar, so its scale is 500000.
provider.Source hint: Where this provider gets its credentials. Picking one fills in the type, base URL and models, so a subscription needs nothing typed and a vendor needs only its key.
provider.Switch hint: Point an agent at this provider
provider.Usage hint: Point any client that speaks this provider's API at Gateway with these variables.
provider.Used by no agent: No agent uses this provider yet

setting.API key encryption key hint: Encrypts the provider API keys at rest, any length. Back it up with the database: losing it makes already-encrypted keys unreadable.
setting.Agent record capacity hint: Agent records are never written to disk, so this also bounds the memory they use.
setting.Agent state dir hint: Patch manifests, config backups, ingest tokens and file-tail cursors.
setting.Channel probes description: A probe sends four short requests to a provider's upstream and checks the answers against what the vendor's API documents: the model name reported, the vendor headers carried, the shape of the event stream, whether prompt caching is really accounted for, and whether two identical requests are billed the same. It spends a few cents of that provider's own credit.
setting.LLM records description: Prompts can carry sensitive data, so anything beyond metadata is opt-in.
setting.Outbound SOCKS5 proxy hint: "host:port", used for outbound traffic such as update downloads.
setting.Page description: Everything Casbin Gateway reads out of its configuration. Changes are stored in the database and applied at once.
setting.Pricing file hint: Optional JSON file of token prices in US dollars per million, overriding the built-in list prices.
setting.Probe mode hint: Automatic probing runs when a provider is added, when its endpoint, type or key changes, and once for any provider that has never been probed.
setting.Queue capacity hint: A full queue drops records rather than slowing the proxy down.
setting.Relay token hint: What an agent sends to /v1. Requests from this machine never need it. Clear the field and save to issue a new one.
setting.Sign-in description: Casdoor is optional: leave the endpoint empty to sign in against Gateway's own user table.

usage.Agents description: What the agents on this machine spent, read from the transcripts they write themselves. This is the only account of a request that never went through Gateway.
usage.Cache write 1h hint: Only Anthropic sells a cache that lives an hour. Zero means every write is charged at the rate above.
usage.Cache writes are not reported by every p: A provider serving the OpenAI protocol reports cache hits but never cache writes, so this can read as zero while the cache is being written.
usage.Delete this price detail: There is no built-in price for this model, so requests using it stop being costed until a price is set again.
usage.Import from models.dev description: Pick a model to copy its published rates into the form. models.dev lists the same model under every provider reselling it, so each rate here is the one most of them agree on.
usage.Model key hint: Matched as a substring of the name a request arrives under, so "claude-opus-5" also prices "claude-opus-5-20260214".
usage.Model pricing description: What a million tokens costs, which is what every figure on the Usage page is worked out from. A price stored here overrides the built-in list price for that model.
usage.Nothing was spent in this window: Nothing was spent in this window
usage.Price dialog description: Rates are in US dollars per million tokens. A price saved here is yours from then on, and a models.dev sync will leave it alone.
usage.Priced {updated} of {considered} models: Priced {updated} of the {considered} models this machine has run
usage.Put the built-in price back detail: The stored price is dropped and the built-in list price for this model takes effect again. Records already costed keep the figures they were costed at.
usage.Rates are per million tokens: All five rates are in US dollars per million tokens.
usage.Read from a catalogue of {count} models: Read from a models.dev catalogue of {count} models.
usage.Recording is off detail: llmRecordMode is "off", so nothing relayed is being counted. The agents' own transcripts are counted either way.
usage.Relayed description: What Gateway relayed on behalf of the agents. This is the only account that knows which provider answered, and whether it failed.
